guides.title: Test real runtime auth, policy, RPC and hydration
guides.summary: Inject production app.fetch or the generated Worker fetch into createServerApp. The helper sends real Request objects through that handler; it does not implement alternate routing, authorization, DI or cleanup. authFixture supplies headers/cookies only. Authentication middleware and policy must decide whether credentials are valid.
guides.markdown:
Inject production app.fetch or the generated Worker fetch into createServerApp. The helper sends real Request objects through that handler; it does not implement alternate routing, authorization, DI or cleanup. authFixture supplies headers/cookies only. Authentication middleware and policy must decide whether credentials are valid.

componentRpc sends the production /crpc envelope. serviceRpc identifies the declaring owner, service slot, and the page (componentRouteId plus pageParams) whose guards run before the service. Public state remains untrusted input. Use authorized and denied fixtures and assert actual effects/cleanup, not only HTTP status. readHydrationState parses the JSON assignment without evaluating JavaScript. Generated Node/workerd/browser acceptance verifies the compiler, real auth/policy, service cleanup, hydration and server-code stripping; a synthetic fetch closure cannot prove those behaviors.

This reusable contract test accepts the real generated fetch handler and fixture route IDs. Run it against an application whose protected /account route and ping RPC use the supplied test session.

guides.title: Control concurrent request scopes and cleanup
guides.summary: withRequestScope binds the core request/DI facilities and awaits scope disposal in finally. It does not scope the framework configuration store; inject the production fetch handler for config middleware acceptance. Declare service ownership rather than resolving arbitrary globals.
guides.markdown:
withRequestScope binds the core request/DI facilities and awaits scope disposal in finally. It does not scope the framework configuration store; inject the production fetch handler for config middleware acceptance. Declare service ownership rather than resolving arbitrary globals.

controlledAsync gives tests deterministic resolve/reject/cancel controls and a finite timeout option. Attach the promise to the operation before cancelling it. This controls test scheduling, not an incoming TCP disconnect. Native disconnect acceptance must use the host's incoming Request.signal.

The example overlaps two explicit user scopes without real timers and waits for both finalizers.

guides.title: Render browser components and await asynchronous teardown
guides.summary: Use render in a browser or DOM test environment. Helpers click/type wait for component updates; unmount awaits destroyAsync and removes the container even on failed cleanup. Pass public hydration state and props explicitly. A service scope supplied without ownsServiceScope stays caller-owned.
guides.markdown:
Use render in a browser or DOM test environment. Helpers click/type wait for component updates; unmount awaits destroyAsync and removes the container even on failed cleanup. Pass public hydration state and props explicitly. A service scope supplied without ownsServiceScope stays caller-owned.

DOM simulations cover component behavior, not keyboard/native file controls, real navigation, hydration node identity, or compiler stripping. Use actual generated browser acceptance for those criteria. Keep the browser entry separate from the Node-only server helpers. The exported example function runs only when called in a DOM environment.
